before.title: Claude hacks OpenAI: Security researchers used Anthropic's tool to break into a ChatGPT account
before.body: Cybersecurity researchers broke into an OpenAI employee's ChatGPT account using software from Anthropic, OpenAI's key rival. The team gained access to private software information and even suggested changes, highlighting vulnerabilities in the ChatGPT maker's security posture at a time when leading AI companies face mounting scrutiny over safety. The researchers had been given access to an Anthropic tool specifically designed for security professionals, and were paid for the work as part of a program to find vulnerabilities before bad actors could exploit them. The episode is a reminder that the AI industry's competitive rivalry extends to offensive security: one company's red-team instrument became the lever against another's infrastructure.

before.body: NASA has modified its Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract to add three SpaceX missions—Crew-15, Crew-16 and Crew-17—under a firm fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity modification. The $946 million package covers ground, launch, in-orbit, return and recovery operations, cargo transportation for each mission, and lifeboat capability while docked. after.title: SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway: Fast Routing or Added Complexity?
after.body: Optimist: AWS says its GPU-aware HyperPod Inference Gateway can reduce first-token latency by up to 82 percent. It uses real-time GPU signals to route requests to suitable pods, aiming to reduce idle capacity left unused by naive routing. Skeptic: An additional EKS-managed addon is still another layer to operate; whether the performance benefit justifies that layer depends on the workload.
